facts.statement: Hydrorion fossils were found in the Posidonia Shale of south-western Germany.
facts.quote: It is only known from multiple specimens, all discovered in the Posidonia Shale of south-western Germany.

facts.statement: Hydrorion lived during the Toarcian Age of the Lower Jurassic.
facts.quote: Hydrorion (meaning 'water hunter') is a genus of plesiosaur from the Toarcian Age of the Lower Jurassic.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Hydrorion measured 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small plesiosaur, with the largest specimen measuring 4 m long.

facts.statement: The only species of Hydrorion is H. brachypterygius, which was first described as Plesiosaurus and later as Microcleidus.
facts.quote: The only species of Hydrorion is H. brachypterygius, which was originally described as a species of Plesiosaurus and then Microcleidus.

facts.statement: The genus Hydrorion was named by Großmann in 2007.
Hydrorion belongs to the family Plesiosauridae.
